title: A Inventory for the Weather
premise: Rosalind Coldharbour, a translator whose childhood language is dissolving word by word, has spent decades keeping an inventory of everything her family never said. At her mother's funeral, a stranger addresses the family by a name no one uses—revealing that Rosalind's parents lived under an assumed identity, and that Rosalind herself was born on the wrong side of a betrayal in the coastal town of Merrow Point. Returning there, Rosalind uncovers a buried inheritance dispute, a forbidden love her mother abandoned for duty, and the truth that Rosalind's own existence was the price of silence. As the town's last native speakers of the dying language prepare to scatter, Rosalind must choose between preserving the family's careful invisibility and claiming a name, a home, and a self of her own—ending with her translating her mother's final unsent letter aloud in the old tongue, the inventory finally emptied.
about_author: Coral Marchetti is the pen name of a former court interpreter who grew up between two languages and one silence. Her fiction examines how families curate forgetting, and this is her second novel.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Words
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. At her mother's sparse funeral, Rosalind notices she can no longer recall the word for 'grief' in the childhood language she translates from professionally. She catalogs what the eulogies omit. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath composed mourning—the inventory of the unsaid begins to feel like it's winning.

chapters.title: A Name Nobody Uses
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A stranger in a grey coat approaches the family after the service and calls them by the surname 'Verrane.' Her brother Denham denies knowing it; Rosalind recognizes it from a half-erased line in her mother's handwriting. Emotional beat: the ground tilts—the family's careful invisibility cracks open.

chapters.title: Inventory of the Unsaid
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, with flashbacks. She opens her lifelong notebook of unspoken things and finds her mother's own list tucked inside, in the dying language. The two inventories mirror each other. Emotional beat: intimacy with the dead achieved too late, and the first pull toward Merrow Point.

chapters.title: Denham Refuses the Sea
chapters.summary: Denham's POV. Rosalind proposes returning to Merrow Point; Denham, who handles the family's money and silences, refuses—there are documents, he admits, he'd rather stayed buried. Emotional beat: sibling fracture; duty weaponized as love.

chapters.title: Merrow Point in the Off-Season
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She arrives in the shuttered coastal town and finds the house her mother grew up in, boarded but not abandoned—someone pays its taxes. A fisherman recognizes her face before she says a word. Emotional beat: eerie belonging; being seen for the first time.

chapters.title: The Last Speakers
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. At the town's fading cultural hall, she meets three elderly speakers of the language, including Maren, who knew her mother as 'Isla Verrane.' They speak to Rosalind in the old tongue and her fluency surprises even herself. Emotional beat: the language returns like floodwater—joy laced with grief.

chapters.title: What the House Remembers
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She breaks into the boarded house and finds a child's room preserved, a second name on the birth registry, and a locked writing desk. Emotional beat: the discovery that Rosalind was not the only Coldharbour child—or the only one erased.

chapters.title: Denham's Ledger
chapters.summary: Denham's POV. In the city, Denham burns a folder of correspondence but keeps one letter. Flashback reveals their father coerced the family's disappearance to escape a scandal involving the Verrane shipping fortune. Emotional beat: complicity; Denham has spent his life as the family's second wall.

chapters.title: Maren's Testimony
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She recounts the summer Isla Verrane loved a boatbuilder named Edern—love against the family's duty to a dynastic match. When Isla chose duty, Edern's family was ruined. Emotional beat: the romance at the story's heart, told by the one who watched it fail.

chapters.title: The Boatbuilder's Granddaughter
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She tracks down Sef, Edern's granddaughter, who runs the town's last boatyard and wants nothing to do with Verranes. Sef accuses the family of theft—the yard's deed, she says, was taken. Emotional beat: Rosalind inherits an enemy she didn't choose.

chapters.title: Words for Betrayal
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Digging in town archives, Rosalind finds the transfer papers: her grandfather forged Edern's signature. Worse, her mother witnessed it and stayed silent to protect her engagement. Emotional beat: the mother Rosalind mourned becomes a stranger; power's corruption made intimate.

chapters.title: The Locked Desk
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She returns to the house with Maren's help and opens the writing desk: inside, her mother's unsent letters to Edern, forty years of them, written in the old language and addressed to 'my daughter, whoever she becomes.' Emotional beat: devastating tenderness—the inventory was always meant for Rosalind.

chapters.title: Denham Arrives
chapters.summary: Denham's POV. Denham appears in Merrow Point, having traced Rosalind, and demands she come home. He reveals their father's death was no accident of weather—he was running from the Verrane heirs who wanted the forgery buried permanently. Emotional beat: fear enters the story; the past is not finished with them.

chapters.title: The Heirs of Verrane
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A lawyer representing the shipping fortune arrives, offering money for silence about the forged deed—and hinting at what happened to those who refused before. Emotional beat: power's corruption made explicit; Rosalind understands why her parents chose invisibility.

chapters.title: Sef at the Waterline
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef tells Rosalind about her grandfather Edern's slow unraveling after Isla left, and shows her the boat he was building for their escape—still rotting in the shed. Emotional beat: grief answered with grief; the two heirs of the betrayal recognize each other.

chapters.title: A Proposal of Restitution
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind proposes returning the yard's deed to Sef publicly, exposing the Verrane name and ending the family's invisibility forever. Denham threatens to disown her; Maren warns the old heirs have long memories. Emotional beat: the choice crystallizes—safety or selfhood.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Storm
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. During a storm, the lawyer's threats escalate—Denham's car is run off the road, minor injuries. Rosalind reads her mother's final unsent letter and finds Isla planned to confess the forgery before she died. Emotional beat: the mother's unfinished duty passes to her daughter; resolve hardens.

chapters.title: Denham Breaks
chapters.summary: Denham's POV. Recovering, Denham finally reads the letter Rosalind shows him and collapses into the truth he's policed his whole life. He confesses he knew about the forged deed since he was nineteen and chose the money. Emotional beat: the wall comes down; brother and sister reunited in shared failure.

chapters.title: The Gathering at the Hall
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The town gathers for the cultural hall's closing—perhaps the last assembly of native speakers. Rosalind stands before them as a Verrane and a Coldharbour both. Emotional beat: the climax approaches on a tide of community; identity chosen in public.

chapters.title: Reading Aloud
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Before the assembled town, Sef, and the Verrane lawyer, Rosalind reads her mother's letters aloud in the dying language and formally returns the deed to Sef, naming the forgery and the theft. Emotional beat: the climax—the inventory of the unsaid spoken at last, at real cost.

chapters.title: What the Lawyer Cannot Buy
chapters.summary: Rosalind's and Denham's alternating POV. The Verrane heirs retaliate with lawsuits and offers, but the town's testimony and the letters make denial impossible; the fortune settles rather than face court. Denham chooses to stay in Merrow Point. Emotional beat: consequences land, but the family survives them—power blunted by truth.

chapters.title: An Inventory, Emptied
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, epilogue-like. A year later, Rosalind lives in the reopened house, teaching the language to the hall's small surviving class; Sef's yard builds its first new boat in decades. Rosalind writes one final entry in her inventory notebook and closes it. Emotional beat: resolution—identity claimed, love chosen over duty, the silence finally translated.
